question.text: What is the relationship between call and put deltas for the same strike and expiry?

answer.text: Call delta - Put delta = 1 (approximately). For example, if call delta = 0.60, put delta = -0.40. This follows from put-call parity
Call delta = Put delta (they are always equal)
Call delta + Put delta = 0 (they always cancel out)
There is no mathematical relationship between call and put deltas

explanation.text: The Logic: For European options on the same underlying with the same strike and expiry, put-call parity links the call and put prices: C - P = S - PV(K). Differentiating both sides with respect to the underlying gives the corresponding delta identity: Δ_call - Δ_put = 1, equivalently Δ_put = Δ_call - 1. So if the call delta is 0.60, the put delta is approximately -0.40. The Trap: Call and put deltas at the same strike are not equal in magnitude with the same sign (so they are not literally equal), nor are they exact negatives of each other that "cancel out to zero". And there is a well-defined relationship between them — it is not "no relationship". Note: The NISM Series IV (Interest Rate Derivatives) workbook page reviewed supports put-call parity as a price relationship between a put and a call with the same underlying, strike, and expiry, but the explicit delta-parity identity (call delta - put delta = 1) was not located in the workbook pages reviewed. The derivation above is presented as general options-theory industry knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
